title: Fixed costs, variable costs and break-even
summary: Separating costs by how they behave with sales tells you how much you need to sell.

sections.heading: Fixed and variable
paragraphs: Fixed costs don't change with sales volume in the short term: insurance, property taxes, amortization, permanent staff. "Fixed" doesn't mean they never change, just that they don't depend directly on how much you sell.
Variable costs go up and down with sales: raw materials, beverages, VAT, gross income tax, health & safety levy and card fees.

Labor is a special case: within a month it's almost all fixed (waiters are hired before you know whether customers will come), so it's considered semi-fixed. In catering, by contrast, much of it is variable.

sections.heading: Sales, costs and profit
paragraphs: Net sales = variable costs + fixed costs + profit.

sections.heading: Contribution
paragraphs: What's left of each sale after paying variable costs is the contribution: what it adds toward fixed costs and profit.
Once past the break-even point, every extra dollar of sales generates a profit equal to its contribution. The same formula shows quickly the impact of raising or lowering costs or prices.
